summary: Correct, minimal noop guard equivalent to the accepted Django fix: when old and new db_table match, database_forwards returns early (and database_backwards delegates to it, so both directions are covered). No correctness or regression concerns; only minor readability/comment nits.

issues.description: Condition inlines `from_state.apps.get_model(app_label, self.old_name)._meta.db_table` rather than binding `old_db_table`/`new_db_table` locals; long expression is harder to read and the old_model lookup is duplicated with the line below the guard.
No comment explaining why the early return is a noop (e.g. 'Don't alter when the table name is unchanged'); a one-line comment would clarify intent for future maintainers.
Guard placed before the `allow_migrate_model` check instead of inside it as in the surrounding pattern; outcome is identical (noop in all combinations) but placement differs slightly from repo idiom.
